question: Is the documented fail-closed `update_partial` plus status/Doctor/fresh-plan recovery model acceptable for the first experimental `claws update` release after exact-head package and Gateway failure evidence is supplied?
rationale: No source-only review can decide whether preserving uncertain provenance and requiring operator recovery is an acceptable product contract for mutations that cross independent installer, config, and Gateway boundaries.

options.title: Require recovery proof before merge
options.body: Keep the partial-state design, but require redacted exact-head runs that exercise real package replacement and Gateway cron convergence/failure plus the operator recovery path.

options.title: Accept the experimental recovery contract
options.body: Merge after the parent stack lands while explicitly accepting that external side effects may require manual status/Doctor inspection and a fresh plan.

options.title: Pause apply semantics
options.body: Keep the read-only planner and defer mutation until operation-identity reconciliation or stronger recovery guarantees are designed.

recommendation.title: Require recovery proof before merge
recommendation.body: Keep the partial-state design, but require redacted exact-head runs that exercise real package replacement and Gateway cron convergence/failure plus the operator recovery path.

likelyOwner.reason: Their existing review identifies the precise recovery and operator-experience tradeoff that requires a maintainer decision.
